text:
anya: quick design check — during today's demo people got stuck when reordering rules in the policies editor. dragging looked smooth but they couldn't tell which rule would become active first. screen recording: https://play.redwood/infer/rec/12345 :eyes:
sam: saw that — i think the main issue is the visual affordance for priority. when you drag the card it doesn't show the final index until you drop it. maybe show a live badge like `Priority: #2` that follows the card?
leo: can repro. also current copy on validation modal is terse: 'invalid rule' and people ask "why?". suggest adding inline hint with the expression and the failing token.
anya: agreed on copy. here are two quick options for the validation copy: 1) "Rule invalid: unmatched parentheses in match expression" 2) "Rule can't be applied: use `contains(...)` or `equals(...)` instead of bare strings" — which feels clearer?
morgan: option 1 is better for syntax errors, option 2 is better for semantic guidance. also accessibility: keyboard users need a way to reorder without drag. add up/down chevrons and a live region announcement: "Rule 'User tier' moved to position 2" :a11y:
sam: yes to chevrons. also we should persist the priority number badge even when the card is expanded — it's the anchor.
leo: small UX nit: preview simulation currently only shows the post-routing output. can we add a stepper so you can toggle "evaluate as" with example requests and see which rule matched and what action applied? designbot: preview run for sample input "user.email contains '@enterprise.com'" -> matched rule id=rg-12 priority=1 action=route:dedicated :gear:
anya: that designbot line is gold, we should surface that in the UI: a compact history line per preview run: "Matched: rg-12 (Priority 1) — routed to: dedicated". lightweight and scanable.
morgan: also ensure the matched token is highlighted in the sample request for low-vision users (high contrast + focus ring). keyboard focus should go to the highlighted match after preview runs.
sam: copy follow-up: change the modal button from "Fix" to "See details" for validation errors so it's less prescriptive.
leo: dev question — reordering currently operates on client only until save. people tried to reorder and left, assuming it persisted. we should add a subtle toast: "Order changes saved" or "Order changes not saved" depending on autosave.
anya: good point. proposal: two modes: explicit save (button) for power users, or an autosave toggle in settings. default to explicit with a non-modal toast asking to save when navigating away.
sam: can we run a quick hallway test with 5 people tomorrow? gather 3 mins of task-based feedback: reorder, fix a validation error, run preview.
morgan: i'll add keyboard test checklist: tab order, up/down reordering, screenreader announce messages, contrast checks.
leo: engineering: i'll mock up the live priority badge and preview stepper; i'll paste a screenshot later.
anya: thanks all — next steps: leo prototype + morgan accessibility checklist + sam arrange hallway test. tagging follow-ups here when ready. :thumbsup:
